slot.brief: Compare a given trajectory equation y = ax – bx² with the standard form to extract the angle of projection.

stem: A projectile moves over level ground without air resistance. Its trajectory is $y = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{3}} - \dfrac{x^2}{15}$, where $x$ and $y$ are in metres. The angle of projection to the horizontal is:

verdicts.working: Comparing with y = x tan(theta) - [g/(2u^2 cos^2(theta))]x^2 gives tan(theta) = 1/sqrt(3), so theta = 30 degrees.

working:
$y=x\tan\theta-\dfrac{g x^2}{2u^2\cos^2\theta}$
$\tan\theta=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$
$\therefore\ \theta=30^\circ$

Independent check: Comparing with y = x tan(theta) - [g/(2u^2 cos^2(theta))]x^2 gives tan(theta) = 1/sqrt(3), so theta = 30 degrees.
solution:
The projectile trajectory is $y=x\tan\theta-\dfrac{g x^2}{2u^2\cos^2\theta}$, so the coefficient of $x$ gives
$$\tan\theta=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\implies\theta=30^\circ.$$

draft.stem: A projectile moves over level ground without air resistance. Its trajectory is $y = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{3}} - \dfrac{x^2}{15}$, where $x$ and $y$ are in metres. The angle of projection to the horizontal is:
draft.distractor_notes: A: Confuses the coefficient with an angle in radians or misreads it. B: Correct. C: Assumes equal horizontal and vertical projection components. D: Uses the reciprocal of the coefficient as the tangent.
